title: Why Can't You TICKLE Yourself? (Try It Now) 🤭
description:
Try to tickle your own palm right now. Nothing, right? Your brain read the spoiler. Every time you move, it keeps a copy of the order and predicts exactly where your finger will land, so the touch arrives with no surprise and the brain turns the feeling down. Someone else's finger comes with no warning, and you fall apart. Scientists in London showed it with two robots: people moved a handle with one hand while a soft foam tip copied the movement on their other palm. Moved in sync, it barely tickled. With a delay of a fifth of a second, it felt as tickly as someone else's touch, and most people never noticed the delay. Did it tickle?
